name: Flask render_template_string with dynamic template (SSTI)
attack_scenario: name = "{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}" lands in the template body; Jinja2 evaluates it and returns command output and SECRET_KEY, chaining to full RCE.
negative_test_hint: submit name = "{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}" and assert the response renders it as inert text with no command output

exemplar.explanation: Flask's render_template_string() compiles its FIRST argument as a Jinja2 template. Jinja2 evaluates {{...}} expressions with full Python object access, so any user input reaching the template source (via f-string, %, +, .format(), or a request value spliced positionally) is server-side template injection, escalating past XSS to code execution in the app process. It is safe only when user data is passed as context kwargs, as in render_template_string(TEMPLATE, name=request.args['name']).
